page: OVHcloud r3-256 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 256 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for several resource-intensive operations. The AMD EPYC processor achieves strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 98,466.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 63,623.58. Memory performance is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 4,744.5 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 135.71 GB/sec. Database operations are highly optimized, with Redis SET operations executing at 75.95 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring 30,782.6.

While the instance excels in memory-intensive tasks and multi-threaded decompression, single-threaded performance is more moderate, with gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into average performance tiers. The lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it demonstrates strong performance for small-scale LLM inference. Given its high memory density and strong database benchmarks, the r3-256 is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
